title: Cross-WIN H(r)/FSF/B(r) terminology standardization (ISS-2952 follow-through on WIN-040 c5)
target: Standardize the H(r)=firmament-height / FSF=H(r)/r / B(r)=toroidal-field terminology frame across the canonical Axial Symmetry Paradox section (data/sections.json part2 #axial-symmetry) and the three WINs that independently mislabel H(r) as a "field equation" (WIN-041, WIN-043, WIN-059).
investigation_summary: ISS-2952 asked for a coordinated cross-WIN terminology pass covering WIN-040, WIN-053, and any other WIN invoking axial symmetry, per curmudgeon c5 finding (c) on WIN-040. Checked the decider run that created ISS-2952 (decider-2026-07-08T02-08): the WIN-040-specific fixes (ISS-2950 moderate FSF/B(r) parenthetical, ISS-2951 minor centre/boundary hedge) were already self-applied in that same commit — verified in data/wins.json WIN-040.detail_evidence, which now reads "...primary geometric (firmament-height) function H(r) = 8537*exp(-r/8619) (and the derived field-strength factor FSF = H(r)/r used for the domes geomagnetic-magnitude predictions elsewhere...along with the toroidal field function B(r)=A*e^(-r_N/lambda)+C*e^(-r_S/lambda) used in WIN-053)..." -- this already implements the standardized frame (a) H(r)=firmament-height (b) FSF=H(r)/r (c) B(r) quoted from WIN-053. WIN-053 independently already ties H(r) and B(r) together correctly via the shared lambda=8,619 km scale length. So the two WINs named explicitly in ISS-2952 are DONE. The remaining scope is "check any other WIN invoking axial symmetry" (c5 notes explicitly instruct this). Traced the canonical hub: 12+ WINs (WIN-004,005,006/007,024,028,035,036,040,041,043,059,060,063) all cross-link to data/sections.json #axial-symmetry ("2.10 The Axial Symmetry Paradox") rather than each independently re-deriving the point. That section itself currently mislabels H(r) as the domes "core field equation" / "core equation" (ps-tldr and opening line) -- exactly the mislabel curmudgeon flagged for WIN-040, but sitting at the one place all the other WINs actually point to. Fixing this canonical section once propagates the correct frame to every WIN that links there, which is more efficient and more consistent than 12 separate per-WIN patches, and matches the c5 recommendation to roll this into a single pass rather than a narrow find/replace. Independently grepped both data files for the literal mislabel pattern (H(r) called "field equation") and found 3 WIN-level instances beyond the section itself: WIN-041 (detail_verdict_text), WIN-043 (detail_verdict_text), WIN-059 (detail_evidence) -- all three link to #axial-symmetry and independently repeat the same "field equation H(r)" phrasing rather than "firmament-height equation H(r)". These are the residual cross-WIN drift instances ISS-2952 was scoped to catch. No verdict changes anywhere -- this is pure terminology tightening to preempt the semantic-swap defender move documented in WIN-040.c5 advocate_mode (defense_survives:3), applied at its structural root plus the three WINs that independently repeat the old phrasing.

patches.find_pattern: The dome's core equation H(r) = 8,537 × exp(−r/8,619) depends only on radial distance — it has no longitude variable.
patches.replace_pattern: The dome's core geometric (firmament-height) equation H(r) = 8,537 × exp(−r/8,619) depends only on radial distance — it has no longitude variable.
patches.description: TLDR of 2.10 Axial Symmetry Paradox calls H(r) the domes "core equation" with no qualifier, inviting the same field-equation-swap ambiguity curmudgeon flagged on WIN-040. Labels it firmament-height explicitly, matching the frame already shipped in WIN-040.

patches.find_pattern:
The dome's core field equation is:

H(r) = 8,537 × exp(−r / 8,619) km
patches.replace_pattern:
The dome's core geometric (firmament-height) equation is:

H(r) = 8,537 × exp(−r / 8,619) km

Two quantities derived from H(r) inherit this same radial-only dependence: the field-strength factor FSF = H(r)/r used for magnetometer-station predictions (e.g. WIN-025), and the toroidal field equation B(r) = A·e−rN/λ + C·e−rS/λ used in WIN-053. "H(r)," "FSF," and "B(r)" are three different equations serving three different purposes (firmament height, field-strength scaling, and two-pole magnetic fit respectively) — but all three are axially symmetric by construction, so a defender cannot rescue a longitude-dependent claim by pointing to a different one of the three.
patches.description: Root-cause fix: this is the canonical section 12+ WINs link to via #axial-symmetry rather than re-deriving the point per-WIN. Naming H(r)/FSF/B(r) here once, with the standardized frame from WIN-040.c5, closes the semantic-swap defense for every WIN that cross-references this section, not just WIN-040/WIN-053.

patches.find_pattern: its field equation H(r)=8537·exp(−r/8619) depends only on radial distance and is azimuthally symmetric
patches.replace_pattern: its firmament-height equation H(r)=8537·exp(−r/8619) depends only on radial distance and is azimuthally symmetric
patches.description: WIN-041 independently repeats the "field equation H(r)" mislabel found on WIN-040 pre-patch. Aligns with the standardized firmament-height label.

patches.find_pattern: The dome's H(r) field equation depends only on radial distance from the disc center
patches.replace_pattern: The dome's H(r) firmament-height equation depends only on radial distance from the disc center
patches.description: WIN-043 independently repeats the "field equation" mislabel for H(r) (this WIN already correctly labels B(r) separately in the same sentence — only the H(r) mention needs the fix).

patches.find_pattern: the dome's field equation H(r)=8,537·exp(−r/8,619) is axially symmetric
patches.replace_pattern: the dome's firmament-height equation H(r)=8,537·exp(−r/8,619) is axially symmetric
patches.description: WIN-059 independently repeats the "field equation" mislabel for H(r), same pattern as WIN-040 pre-patch, WIN-041, WIN-043.

anticipated_objections.objection: Why patch the canonical section instead of touching WIN-053 to explicitly reference FSF too, per the literal (a)/(b)/(c) frame in the c5 note?
anticipated_objections.response: WIN-053 does not discuss magnetometer-station predictions at all (that is WIN-025/WIN-010 territory) -- forcing an FSF mention into WIN-053 would be an off-topic insertion. WIN-053 already correctly ties H(r) and B(r) together via the shared lambda=8,619 km scale length, which is the only cross-reference it actually needs. The (a)/(b)/(c) frame is fully realized across the corpus: WIN-040 states all three, WIN-053 states H(r)+B(r), and the newly-patched section 2.10 states all three centrally for every other linking WIN.

anticipated_objections.objection: Should every one of the 12+ WINs listed in section 2.10 get an individual patch instead of relying on the linked section?
anticipated_objections.response: No -- that is the narrow find/replace approach c5 explicitly said not to do ("Not a single narrow find/replace" per the ISS routing_reason). The 3 WIN-level patches here are only for WINs that independently repeat the exact mislabeled phrase (verified via grep across data/wins.json); WINs that merely link to #axial-symmetry without repeating the phrase (WIN-004, 005, 006/007, 024, 028, 035, 036, 060, 063 etc.) inherit the fix automatically once the linked section is corrected, with no per-WIN edit needed or wanted.

new_evidence_added: None -- pure terminology/labeling patch, no new citations or claims. All five patches are word-level relabeling ("field equation" -> "firmament-height equation" for H(r) specifically) plus one explanatory addition (PATCH-2) that only restates facts already present elsewhere in the corpus (FSF=H(r)/r per WIN-025/WIN-040; B(r) per WIN-053).
holes_addressed: WIN-040.c5 hole (c) minor -- cross-WIN terminology divergence with WIN-053, extended to cover the canonical Axial Symmetry Paradox section plus 3 other WINs found to independently repeat the same mislabel.
test_coverage: No numeric/data-blob values changed -- all patches are string relabeling within existing HTML prose (detail_verdict_text, detail_evidence, and sections.json part2.html). tests/run.sh does not check this prose content for specific wording; node test.js pass/fail is unaffected by these patches. Ran node -e JSON.parse sanity check on both data/wins.json and data/sections.json after simulating each patch locally before writing this EXP (see notes).
notes: PROP-034 Phase 1 BAU drain.
